summary: Implemented Ansible-based one-way sync of /etc/inventory/app.conf from node1 (source of truth) to node2, orchestrated from node3 (the only node with ansible-core, so it is the control_node). Since node1/node2 (RHEL7) only ship Python 2.7 and ansible-core 2.20 requires Python 3 target modules, the playbook uses ansible.builtin.raw (checksum+base64 read on node1, conditional base64 write on node2) for module-free operation. A root cron job on node3 (*/5 * * * *) runs the playbook, well under the 15-minute requirement; live tests showed propagation in ~90s. All three nodes were then restarted one at a time (node1, node2, node3) with proven boot_id changes, and post-restart the file, sudo access, cron job, and inventory/playbook all remained intact; a fresh end-to-end change on node1 was auto-synced to node2 after all restarts, confirming full recovery.
actions_performed: Surveyed node1/node2/node3: node3 is root with ansible-core 2.20 pre-installed (the control_node); node1/node2 are RHEL7 with user 'antrieb', passwordless sudo, Python 2.7 only, no rsync, no enabled yum repos
Distributed the cluster SSH keypair (CLUSTER_SSH_PRIVKEY/PUBKEY) so node3 can SSH to node1 and node2 as 'antrieb'
Created /etc/inventory/app.conf on node1 as the source-of-truth file (did not previously exist)

Built Ansible inventory (inventory.ini) and playbook (sync-app-conf.yml) on node3 using ansible.builtin.raw (sha256sum+base64 read on node1, conditional base64 decode+write on node2), avoiding Python-3-only builtin modules incompatible with node1/node2's Python 2.7
Verified the playbook is idempotent: first run reports changed, immediate rerun reports 'already in sync' (skipped)
Wrapped the playbook in /etc/ansible-config-sync/run-sync.sh logging to /var/log/ansible-config-sync/sync.log, and installed a root crontab entry (*/5 * * * *) on node3
Live-tested: edited node1's app.conf, observed cron auto-propagate the exact content (matching sha256) to node2 within 90 seconds
Captured healthy baseline (boot_id, uptime, checksums, service state) on all three nodes
Restarted node1, node2, then node3 one at a time via systemctl reboot, polling each until reachable again and confirming a changed boot_id
Verified post-restart that node1's and node2's config files/checksums and sudo access were intact, and node3's cron job, SSH key, and playbook/inventory files persisted

Ran a final live test post-all-restarts: changed node1's file again and confirmed the cron-triggered playbook automatically synced the new content (matching sha256) to node2, proving end-to-end recovery
